question: Isosceles triangle \(ABC\) has \(AB = AC = 3\sqrt6,\) and a circle with radius \(5\sqrt2\) is tangent to line \(AB\) at \(B\) and to line \(AC\) at \(C.\) What is the area of the circle that passes through vertices \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C?\)
solution:
Let \(O\) be the center of the given circle. A radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent, so \(\angle ABO\) and \(\angle ACO\) are both right angles. Therefore \(B\) and \(C\) lie on the circle with diameter \(AO\): a point sees a diameter under a right angle. This is the circle through \(A,B,C\), shown in [Figure 1](figures/2021_Fall_AMC_10A_Q15_official_solution_fig1.png).

Right triangle \(ABO\) gives
\[
AO^2=AB^2+BO^2=(3\sqrt6)^2+(5\sqrt2)^2=54+50=104.
\]
The desired radius is half of \(AO\), so its square is \(104/4=26\). The circle's area is \(\boxed{26\pi}\), choice C.
